en: Krishna said: Kaunteya, this body is called the field. Those who know these things call the one who knows it the knower of the field.

first: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत ।
en: Know me also as the knower of the field in all fields, Bharata. The knowledge of the field and of its knower is, in my view, true knowledge.

first: तत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च यद्विकारि यतश्च यत् ।
en: Hear from me in brief what the field is, what it is like, how it changes and where it comes from; and who its knower is and what his power is.
Sages have sung of this in many ways and in various separate hymns, and it is settled in the reasoned and firm words of the Brahma Sutras.
The great elements, the sense of 'I', the intellect and the unseen nature; the ten senses and the mind; and the five fields of the senses;

first: इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं संघातश्चेतना धृतिः ।
en: desire, dislike, pleasure, pain, the body as a whole, awareness and steadiness: this, in brief, is the field with its changes.
Humility, freedom from pretence, non-violence, patience, honesty, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness and self-control;
lack of craving for sense objects, absence of ego, and seeing clearly the trouble and pain of birth, death, old age and disease;
freedom from attachment, not clinging to children, wife, home and the like, and an even mind at all times whether wanted or unwanted things happen;
undivided, unwavering devotion to me through single-minded yoga, a liking for quiet places, and no taste for crowds;
constant attention to knowledge of the Self, and keeping in view the purpose of knowing the truth: this is called knowledge. Whatever is opposed to it is ignorance.
I will tell you what is to be known, knowing which one gains immortality. It is the beginningless supreme Brahman, said to be neither being nor non-being.
Its hands and feet are everywhere; its eyes, heads and mouths are everywhere; its ears are everywhere. It exists in the world, covering all things.
It seems to have the qualities of all the senses, yet it is without any senses. It is unattached, yet it supports all. It is beyond the gunas, yet it experiences them.
It is outside and inside all beings, unmoving and also moving. Being so subtle, it cannot be grasped. It is far away and also very near.

first: अविभक्तं च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् ।
en: It is undivided, yet it seems divided among beings. Know it as the one who sustains beings, who swallows them up and who brings them forth.
It is the light of all lights and is said to be beyond darkness. It is knowledge, what is to be known, and what is reached by knowledge; it lives in the heart of everyone.

first: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः ।
en: So the field, knowledge and what is to be known have been told in brief. My devotee who understands this becomes fit for my state of being.
Know that nature (prakriti) and the Person (purusha) are both without beginning. Know also that all changes and the gunas are born of nature.
Nature is said to be the cause of the body and the senses and of their action. The Person is said to be the cause of the experience of pleasure and pain.
The Person, living in nature, experiences the gunas born of nature. Attachment to the gunas is the cause of its births in good and bad wombs.
The supreme Person in this body is also called the witness, the one who approves, the supporter, the one who experiences, the great Lord and the highest Self.

first: य एवं वेत्ति पुरुषं प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सह ।
en: Whoever knows the Person and nature with its gunas in this way is not born again, however they may live.
Some see the Self in themselves through meditation, by their own mind; others by the path of knowledge (Sankhya), and others by the yoga of action.
Still others, not knowing this, worship after hearing it from others. They too, devoted to what they have heard, go beyond death.
Whatever being is born, moving or unmoving, know, best of the Bharatas, that it comes from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
Whoever sees the supreme Lord living equally in all beings, the undying within the dying, truly sees.
Seeing the same Lord present equally everywhere, one does not harm the Self by the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
Whoever sees that all actions are done in every way by nature alone, and that the Self is not the doer, truly sees.
When one sees that the separate existence of beings rests in the One, and that all of them spread out from it alone, one then becomes Brahman.
Being without beginning and beyond the gunas, this highest Self never changes. Though it lives in the body, Kaunteya, it neither acts nor is stained.
As space, present everywhere, is not stained because it is so subtle, so the Self, present everywhere in the body, is not stained.
As the one sun lights up this whole world, so the owner of the field lights up the whole field, Bharata.
Those who see with the eye of knowledge the difference between the field and its knower, and the freeing of beings from nature, reach the highest.
